issues.legal_issue: A building licensed for business remains covered premises even when its use is necessarily combined with separately licensed machinery and equipment.
material_facts: The agreement licensed the use of studios and other premises together with machinery and equipment for producing films.
The licensee occupied the studios under an agreement that remained in force when the statutory rule deeming certain licensees to be tenants took effect.
issues.conclusion: The studios and other premises were premises given on licence for business and were covered by the Act, notwithstanding the composite nature of the agreement and the accompanying machinery and equipment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5(4A), 5(8), 5(8A), 6(1) and 15A of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, read together, include a building licensed for business and deem a qualifying licensee to be a tenant. The dominant-purpose approach in Uttamchand v. S. M. Lalwani and Dwarka Prasad v. Dwarka Das Saraf was inapplicable because those cases concerned leases, not a statutory scheme that expressly includes licensed buildings and deems licensees to be tenants.

predicates.business_use_license_case: The proceeding concerns whether rent-control protection applies to a building occupied under a licence for business use.
predicates.building_licensed_for_business: A licensor gave a licensee the use of a building for carrying on a business there.
predicates.licensee_occupied_building_at_transition: The licensee occupied the building when the applicable statutory rule for deeming qualifying licensees to be tenants took effect.

issues.definition: When a business-use licence covers a building and the licensee occupied it when the applicable tenancy rule took effect, rent-control protection covers the building.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory rent forum must determine a covered possession dispute when the claimed relationship is that of landlord and tenant, including when that relationship is contested.
material_facts: The licensee claimed tenant protection in respect of the licensed studios and other premises.
The dispute concerned the right to possession of those premises, and the licensor disputed the claimed protection.
The agreement was in force when the licensee became a deemed tenant under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The Court of Small Causes had jurisdiction to determine the dispute and the parties’ status; the dispute could not be diverted merely because the claimed landlord-tenant relationship was contested.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, gives the specified rent forum jurisdiction over covered landlord-tenant possession disputes and excludes other courts from dealing with them. Jurisdictional facts must be determined by the court before which the jurisdictional question arises. Babulal Bhuramal & Anr. v. Nandram Shivram & Ors. held that a suit does not cease to be one between landlord and tenant merely because the relationship is denied. Raizada Topandas & Anr. v. M/s Gorakhram Gokalchand, Vasudev Gopalkrishna Tamwekar v. The Board of Liquidators, Happy Home Cooperative Housing Society, and Deccan Merchants Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. M/s Dalichand Jugraj Jain & Ors. were also considered in explaining the allocation of jurisdiction.

predicates.rent_control_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns possession of premises in a dispute to which rent-control protection may apply.
predicates.tenant_relationship_claimed: A party claims that the relationship between the parties is that of landlord and tenant, including by operation of a statutory deeming rule.

issues.definition: When a party claims a landlord-tenant relationship in a potentially covered possession dispute, the rent forum determines the relationship and the possession dispute.

issues.legal_issue: Parties cannot use an arbitration agreement to remove a possession dispute covered by the rent-control scheme from the exclusive jurisdiction of the statutory rent forum.
material_facts: The agreement contained an arbitration clause covering disputes between the parties.
The licensee claimed deemed-tenant protection, and the dispute concerned possession of the licensed studios and other premises together with machinery and equipment.
The agreement’s composite character did not change the fact that the studios and other premises had been licensed for business.
issues.conclusion: The Court of Small Causes alone had jurisdiction to decide whether the licensor was entitled to possession; the arbitrator had none, and the arbitration clause was inoperative for the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, both confers jurisdiction on the statutory rent forum and excludes other forums for covered disputes. The Act’s tenant-protection purpose and public policy prevent parties from contracting out of that legislative scheme. The Court relied on Deccan Merchants Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. M/s Dalichand Jugraj Jain & Ors. and considered Babulal Bhuramal & Anr. v. Nandram Shivram & Ors., Raizada Topandas & Anr. v. M/s Gorakhram Gokalchand, and Vasudev Gopalkrishna Tamwekar v. The Board of Liquidators, Happy Home Cooperative Housing Society; Sabavva Kom Hanmappa Simpiger v. Basappa Andaneppa Chiniwar was also directly relevant to the exclusion of arbitration for disputes within section 28.

predicates.rent_control_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns possession of premises in a dispute to which rent-control protection may apply.
predicates.protected_tenant_status: A party occupies the premises with a claimed status protected by the rent-control scheme, including status arising by statutory deeming.
predicates.arbitration_clause_covers_dispute: The parties’ agreement contains an arbitration clause purporting to cover the possession dispute.

issues.definition: If a protected occupant’s possession dispute falls within the rent-control scheme and an arbitration clause purports to cover it, the arbitrator lacks jurisdiction over that dispute.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory rent forum may consider an application to stay a proceeding pending before it without thereby exercising jurisdiction over an arbitration proceeding.
material_facts: A suit concerning the licensed premises was pending in the Court of Small Causes.
The respondent argued that the statutory restriction on that court’s jurisdiction over arbitration proceedings prevented it from staying its own proceeding.
The Court distinguished a request to stay a pending suit from an arbitration proceeding or an application arising out of one.
issues.conclusion: The Court of Small Causes could exercise the power to stay a proceeding pending before it; the restriction on its jurisdiction over arbitration proceedings did not prevent it from considering such a request.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 34 and 40 of the Arbitration Act distinguish an application to stay a proceeding before the judicial authority seized of it from an arbitration proceeding or an application arising out of one. The court relied on the language of those sections and referred to Chadha Motor Transport Co. (P) Ltd., Delhi v. R. N. Chopra and Basanti Cotton Mills v. Dhingra Brothers.

predicates.rent_forum_case_pending: A proceeding concerning a rent-control dispute is pending before the statutory rent forum.
predicates.stay_of_pending_case_sought: A party asks the court handling the pending proceeding to stay it in reliance on an arbitration agreement.

issues.definition: When a rent-control proceeding is pending and a party asks that court to stay it, the rent forum may consider the request.
